Make this a daily habit

Read a little. Recall it. Type it. Change it. Start with five new cards and a few due reviews. Read the explanation, trace the small example, then hide it and reconstruct the idea in Java.

TodayCreates a fixed session of up to five due cards and five unopened cards. It does not automatically mark them mastered.
Again / GoodAgain schedules a next-day review and resets the stage. Good advances through suggested gaps of 1, 3, 7, 14, and 30 days. These are adjustable-by-practice suggestions, not a guarantee of retention.
NavigationUse Previous/Next, left/right arrow keys, or horizontal swipes on the lesson body. Code and diagrams scroll horizontally instead of turning the page. Space reveals the recall answer.
CodeShort fragments teach one idea and may need imports, a method, or surrounding state. The companion ZIP contains complete Java implementations linked by the Run label.
Daily route400 cards at five new cards per session means 80 new-lesson sessions, plus review and coding time. Core has 322 cards; Deep 42; Advanced 36. Take review-only days as needed.
EvidenceAPI contracts link to Oracle. Algorithm references include Princeton, MIT, CMU, and original implementation documentation. Diagrams and lesson prose are original teaching material, not leaked company interview material.
ScopeComprehensive interview preparation, not every possible algorithm or all of Java. JVM tuning, enterprise frameworks, and full concurrency programming are outside this book's main scope. Advanced cards may be recognition-level rather than complete implementations.
StorageNo account or server. Progress is local to this browser, device, and file origin; browser resets or moving the file can make it unavailable. Export regularly. Imports replace local progress after confirmation.

Backup and appearance

Reference edition: 28 September 2026. Java API versions are pinned in source links. Reading and source code do not guarantee interview outcomes; practice fresh problems and explain your reasoning.
